cultural_notes: The Lowcountry has a distinctive building vocabulary: tabby (a coastal material made from oyster shells, lime, and sand), heart pine and cypress from Lowcountry forests, and iron from Charleston's historic forges (source: thecharlestondesigncenter.com Lowcountry Aesthetic; historiccharleston.org)

Charleston brick was fired from local Lowcountry clay in beehive kilns, giving a salmon-pink to deep-red color range; Savannah's counterpart is the soft gray-to-tan handmade Savannah Grey Brick of the early 1800s (source: build-construct.com historic Charleston mansions; americanpavingdesign.com Savannah Grey Brick)
Savannah's historic district is famous for oak-lined squares draped in Spanish moss -- a living museum of American architecture (source: architecturaldigest.com Savannah Historic District)

South Carolina is a peach heavyweight -- the peach is the state fruit and SC ranks second to California in production -- and muscadine, the native Southern grape, appears in late summer (source: discoversouthcarolina.com; positivebloom.com Charleston Farmers Market)

The Gullah Geechee cultural heritage of the Lowcountry coast is significant and should be referenced respectfully; do not appropriate or claim endorsement (source: general cultural knowledge -- honor community sovereignty, no endorsement implied)
